Model a toy car: body is 200x100x100. Subtract 50x100x50 from a top front edge for the windshield. Add four 25-radius, 10-thick wheels aligned at the bottom corners, half embedded into body to form semicylindrical protrusions. | First, describe in words and step by step how the user's request can be implemented using function calls only. After the description, I will ask you to prepare the function call for execution, but don't execute it until I explicitly request it.

Below is the exact construction workflow, expressed step-by-step in plain words and mapped 1-to-1 to the available functions.  
(Only the description is given here; no functions are executed yet.)

1. Car body (initial solid) – one rectangular block  
   • Use block() once with subtraction = False.  
   • Dimensions: x_size = 200, y_size = 100, z_size = 100.  
   • Basepoint: (x, y, z) = (0, 0, 0).  
   • This creates the full 200 × 100 × 100 toy-car body extending in +X, +Y and +Z directions from the global origin.

2. Windshield recess – remove a cuboid from the top-front corner  
   • Call block() a second time with subtraction = True.  
   • Dimensions to remove: x_size = 50, y_size = 100, z_size = 50.  
   • Basepoint (0, 0, 50) means:  
     – it starts flush with the front face (x = 0) and both side faces (y = 0…100)  
     – it occupies the upper half of the body (z = 50…100).  
   • The result is a 50-deep, full-width, top-half cut-out acting as a simple windshield slope.

3. Four wheels – cylinders, half embedded into the body  
   Geometry assumptions  
   • Wheel radius: 25.  
   • Wheel “thickness” (axial length): 10.  
   • Cylinders’ axes are aligned with the Y-axis so wheels roll in the X direction.  
   • Body side planes are at y = 0 (left) and y = 100 (right).  
   • To have each wheel half inside / half outside, place the cylinder’s base 5 mm outside the side face and span 10 mm toward (or away from) the body.

   Cylindrical additions (subtraction = False for all):  

   a) Front-left wheel  
      – baseCenterX = 25 (one radius from front)  
      – baseCenterY = –5 (5 mm outside left face)  
      – baseCenterZ = 25 (radius above ground)  
      – heightVect: (0, 10, 0) → cylinder ends at y = 5, leaving 5 mm inside the body.  

   b) Rear-left wheel  
      – baseCenterX = 175 (200 – 25)  
      – baseCenterY = –5  
      – baseCenterZ = 25  
      – heightVect: (0, 10, 0).  

   c) Front-right wheel  
      – baseCenterX = 25  
      – baseCenterY = 105 (5 mm outside right face)  
      – baseCenterZ = 25  
      – heightVect: (0, –10, 0) so it runs back toward the body, again ending 5 mm inside.  

   d) Rear-right wheel  
      – baseCenterX = 175  
      – baseCenterY = 105  
      – baseCenterZ = 25  
      – heightVect: (0, –10, 0).

   For each cylinder, radius = 25, subtraction = False, cylinder_func = 0 (normal geometry).

4. Closing step  
   • After blocks and cylinders are queued, call finished() with allFunctionsCalled = True.
